sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kishor Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
Heard Sri Ajay Kishor Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rakesh Kumar Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State through video conferencing and perused the material on record.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
She is not named in the first information report.

The other co-accused namely Ajeet Kumar Gupta @ Ajeet Gupta, who is named in the first information report and Smt. Manju Kaushal have already been released on bail by coordinate Bench of this Court, vide orders dated 23.01.2024 and 08.11.2023, passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 813 of 2024 and 13350 of 2023.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 813 of 2024 and 13350 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Copies of bail orders are annexed as Annexure No. 7 to the affidavit filed in support of bail application.
The applicant having identical and similar role to the co-accused, who have already been released on bail is also entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity.

entities.text: Neelam Kaushal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that 49 cases have been registered against the applicant for same incident and the applicant had already granted bail in 30 cases.
There is no chance of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the witnesses and in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
Learned A.G.A. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer of bail.
However, he does not dispute the aforesaid facts.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, from perusal of the record and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment as well as totality of facts and circumstances, at this stage, without commenting on the merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let applicant Neelam Kaushal be released on bail in Case Crime No. 0155 of 2020, under Sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506, 120B I.P.C., registered at P.S. Kumarganj, District Ayodhya,
on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Magistrate/Court concerned, subject to the following conditions:
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant will abide by the orders of the court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant will not indulge in any unlawful activity.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
